business_scope.primary_industry_name: Specialty Fresh Bakery Master Franchise and Central Kitchen Ops

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (based on Swiss Civil Code and Swiss Code of Obligations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (BIT) (signed 1986, in force 1987)
Free Trade Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China (entered into force 1 July 2014)
Convention between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 2013, applicable from 1 January 2014)
Agreement between Switzerland and Hong Kong SAR for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (in force 2010/2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/AMLD) SR 955.0 of 10 October 1997, as amended; Swiss Criminal Code (StGB) SR 311.0; Swiss Code of Obligations (SCO/OR) Articles 697g to 697k (beneficial ownership register obligations for private companies); Federal Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV) SR 221.411; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA) SR 955.033.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each direct shareholder and natural-person beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of country of origin (e.g., Public Security Bureau of the People's Republic of China)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (China and Switzerland are Parties to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of the parent corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of PRC, or Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English/German/French translation of the parent company's business registration and board resolution authorizing incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization + Hague Apostille on the original source document

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / source-of-funds letter for the intended capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank of the shareholder or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if authenticating jurisdiction is not an Apostille member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered address of shareholders (utility bill or government-issued address certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal or utility authority of the shareholder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney in favor of the Swiss incorporation agent / notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent company or fully identified future shareholders

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners and authorized signatories against (i) the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions list, (ii) the Swiss SECO sanctions list (Embargo Act SR 946.211), (iii) the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN list, (iv) the EU restrictive measures list, and (v) a recognized global and Swiss PEP database. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) and source-of-wealth documentation are mandatory for foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs). Screening must be performed pre-incorporation and repeated on an ongoing basis pursuant to FINMA Circular 2023/1 and AMLA Art. 3-6.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex) — the official search portal of the Swiss Commercial Register; formal name clearance and reservation are executed through the competent cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory firm name of an Aktiengesellschaft (AG) must be in one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh) or must be a permissible transliteration in Latin script, and must comply with Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 950. Chinese characters are not permitted in the registered legal name; a Chinese trade name may be recorded as supplementary information only. The name must be distinctive, truthful, and not misleading as to the legal form or business purpose.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Suisse / Schweiz / Helvetia (where implying state sponsorship or deceptive geographic origin)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended in writing prior to expiry at the discretion of the cantonal Commercial Register Office. In case of rejection, the applicant must file a written objection with the competent cantonal Commercial Register Office within ten (10) days of the rejection notice; if the objection is denied, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht) within ten (10) days; a further appeal lies to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court. A new name application may be filed concurrently.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permitted for administrative registered-seat and mail-forwarding purposes only in select cantons, subject to a genuine connection to the canton and availability of physical registered-office services through a licensed fiduciary. For an Aktiengesellschaft operating as a specialty fresh bakery master franchise with a central kitchen, a virtual office is not acceptable as the sole place of registration; the company must maintain a physical Swiss-registered office, and the central kitchen requires operational premises with food-safety and labor compliance filings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for the administrative registered office (approximately 15% probability of unannounced compliance/AML spot checks by cantonal authorities); High for central kitchen and food-processing facilities (approximately 75% probability of unannounced cantonal food-safety, health and labor inspections within the first 12 months of operations).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance, availability search and reservation in the cantonal Commercial Register via Zefix
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (e.g., Commercial Register of the Canton of Zug)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of original Chinese corporate and identity documents (passports, business licensing, certificate of good standing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) of the People's Republic of China / cantonal apostille office in Switzerland

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of Chinese-language corporate, identity and banking documents into German/French/English
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (per page / per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC file compilation, UBO register drafting and PEP/sanctions screening (UN, OFAC, SECO, EU, PEP databases)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss corporate services provider / trustee (Treuhand)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for enhanced due diligence package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of preliminary articles of association and foundation statements (pre-incorporation)
Swiss registered-office administration service (pre-incorporation reservation and correspondence)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual market fee, pro-rated for pre-incorporation period

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account pre-screening, compliance vetting and capital deposit officer application support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Selected Swiss bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or a private bank)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank's internal AML and account-opening administrative fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SHAB (Swiss Official Gazette) name publication reservation and related announcements
Legal review and structured Stage 1 due-diligence memorandum

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620-763 for the Aktiengesellschaft (Stock Company); core incorporation and registration provisions at Arts. 629-642; supplementary Civil Code (ZGB) Art. 52 on legal personality; notarial requirements per Arts. 55, 184 and 634 OR.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of the registered seat (Handelsregisteramt / Office cantonal du registre du commerce)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarially authenticated Deed of Formation and Articles of Association (Errichtungsurkunde & Statuten / Acte constitutif & Statuts), with the Commercial Register entry effecting legal personality
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital is CHF 100,000 fully subscribed (Art. 621 OR). At incorporation at least 20% of the nominal value of shares must be paid in cash, but not less than CHF 50,000 total (Art. 632 OR). The paid-in amount must be deposited into a blocked capital opening account (Kapitaleinlagekonto / Anderkonto) with a FINMA-regulated Swiss bank and must remain at the company's irrevocable disposal, expressly blocked until Commercial Register registration is completed (Art. 633 OR)
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST ORGANIZING RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING BOARD OF [COMPANY] AG 1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: The Articles of Association are confirmed; the share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 nominal value each, is fully subscribed by the founding shareholders, and allocation as per the founding deed is approved. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office is fixed at [street, canton], Switzerland; the Chairman of the Board is authorized to complete the Commercial Register filing and to administer the registered correspondence. 3. OFFICERS: [Name] is appointed Chairman with individual signature; [Name] is appointed Delegate of the Board/Managing Director with individual signature; both mandates are accepted and effective upon registration. Deposited capital is fully available in the blocked account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Preparation and Certification of Formation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary of the canton of the registered seat (Notariat / Étude notariale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association (Statuten) per Art. 626 OR and the Deed of Formation (Errichtungsurkunde) per Art. 629 OR. The notary identifies the founding shareholders, verifies their capacity and nationality, confirms the capital structure and corporate purpose, and authenticates the deed as a public instrument. Verify the corporate name availability with the Commercial Register before notarization.
required_dossiers: Founding shareholders' passports or national IDs
Power of attorney for any authorized representative
Draft Articles of Association complying with Art. 626 OR
Draft Deed of Formation per Art. 629 OR
Beneficial ownership declaration (Form A) and source-of-funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises identification or domicile queries, supply corrective evidence within 10 working days. Material amendments after certification require a fresh notarial act; the original fee is typically credited against re-notarization if the initial dossier is retained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Deposit Account and Minimum Capital Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-regulated Swiss bank with Swiss Bankers Association (SBA) agreement on capital opening accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital opening account (Kapitaleinlagekonto / Anderkonto) in the intended company name at a regulated Swiss bank. Founders remit the statutory paid-in minimum of CHF 50,000 (or higher if the articles so require) into this account. The bank issues a capital deposit attestation (Bankattest / Attestation de provision) confirming that the funds are irrevocably reserved for the company and released only upon Commercial Register registration.
required_dossiers: Certified excerpt of the Deed of Formation and draft Articles
Company name and UID coordination statement
Form A for legal entities with beneficial ownership disclosure
Bank account application and anti-money-laundering declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence due to foreign beneficial ownership, provide bank references, a notarized source-of-funds affidavit, and a personal meeting; if the bank refuses, select an alternative FINMA-regulated institution and promptly obtain a new Bankattest.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitutive Meeting and Appointment of First Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders' constitutive assembly (Generalversammlung der Gründer)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the constitutive meeting, adopt the Articles of Association, and appoint the first Board of Directors. Confirm the subscribed shares and the bank capital attestation. Appoint the auditor whose mandate is required by law or by economic relevance per Art. 727 OR. Execute the written acceptance declarations and specimen signature cards required for registration.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the constitutive shareholders' meeting
Written acceptance of office by each Board member
Auditor's confirmation or waiver per Art. 727a OR
Bank attestation of paid-in capital
Specimen signature forms for registered representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director's appointment is challenged for incapacity, conflict of interest, or regulatory restriction, the general meeting must pass an immediate curative resolution replacing the affected director; the register filing is then amended with the new slate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Dossier with Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office cantonal du registre du commerce)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete notarized incorporation dossier to the Commercial Register of the canton where the registered office is located. The registrar examines compliance with Arts. 640-642 OR, validates the capital attestation and the directors' qualifications, and performs the official name check. The statutory registration fee applies per cantonal tariff and the filing is processed through the official electronic interface or physically at the registry.
required_dossiers: Notarized Deed of Formation and Articles of Association (two originals)
List of Directors with specimen signatures and identification
Bank capital deposit attestation
Share subscription list and founders' declarations
Notification for automatic UID assignment (Federal Statistical Office inputs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency order (Präzisierungsverfügung), respond with the required clarifications within 30 days. Substantively incomplete filings may be withdrawn and resubmitted as a fresh application; an unjustified rejection is appealable to the cantonal supervisory authority within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Acquisition of Legal Personality and Post-Registration Extracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register in cooperation with the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB / FOSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the registrar's examination, the company is entered in the Commercial Register and the entry is gazetted in SHAB/FOSC. Legal personality commences on entry. The blocked capital opening account is released to the company. Obtain the certified Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) confirming company name, capital, seat, directors, and signatory powers.
required_dossiers: Payment receipt of the cantonal registration fee
Certified extract request form
No further substantive dossiers are required at the issuance stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is delayed beyond the SLA, instruct the notary to send a reminder to the registrar; if a formal refusen is issued, appeal to the competent cantonal administrative court within 10 days under cantonal registry procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal UID, VAT, Social Insurance and Employer Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), Cantonal Ausgleichskasse (AHV compensation office), SUVA and the occupational pension institution (BVG/LPP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Federal UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / IDE) is automatically granted upon Commercial Register entry and communicated by the Federal Statistical Office. VAT registration is mandatory once annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 (Art. 51 MWSTG) or on voluntary application for franchising royalty streams. Register as an employer with the cantonal AHV compensation office, take out mandatory accident insurance with SUVA or an approved insurer, and affiliate staff to an occupational pension scheme as required by the BVG/LPP.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract
UID assignment letter from the Federal Statistical Office
VAT registration application (Form 080) where threshold applies
AHV employer registration form
SUVA accident insurance declaration and BVG affiliation statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID is not automatically delivered, contact the UID coordination office (DESO) for manual issuance. If VAT registration is queried on turnover preconditions, submit a voluntary registration and commence filing retroactively. Social insurance forms may be filed electronically with immediate employer recognition through the AHV portal; rectify payroll omissions under the self-disclosure procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cantonal Food Business, Fire and Occupational Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Food Safety Authority (Kantonales Lebensmittelinspektorat) with municipal Fire Prevention Office (Feuerpolizei) and EKAS-accredited occupational safety consultant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notification of a food business operation under Art. 11 of the Foodstuffs and Utility Articles Ordinance (LGV) for the bakery and central kitchen. Prepare the HACCP self-control plan, hygiene registries, and facility layout. Obtain the fire safety inspection approval, the structural load clearance for heavy ovens and equipment, and the workplace operating permit confirming compliance with EKAS safety directives. The cantonal authority issues the operating license that authorizes commencement of production.
required_dossiers: Food business notification form (Meldung / Inscription) under Art. 11 LGV
HACCP self-control plan and cleaning schedule
Premises plan, ventilation, cold storage and equipment specifications
Fire escape plan, fire alarm concept and extinguishing scheme approved by Feuerpolizei
EKAS workplace safety concept (Sicherheitskonzept) and structural load certificate
Food handlers' hygiene certificates (hygiene Pass)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inspection report identifies deficiencies, remediate and request a re-inspection within 10 working days; serious hazards may trigger provisional closure, which must be appealed to the cantonal administrative chamber while interim protective measures are implemented; engage an accredited third-party auditor if the cantonal authority requires independent verification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Food Safety Authority (Lebensmittelinspektorat / Service de la consommation et des affaires vétérinaires) in conjunction with Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/OSAV); municipal Fire Prevention Office (Feuerpolizei); Cantonal Labor Inspectorate for workplace clearance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Betriebsbewilligung / Autorisation d'exploitation for a food production and central kitchen facility under Art. 11 LGV, together with Fire Safety Approval (Brandschutzbewilligung) and Occupational Workplace Operating Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU / OFEV) and the Cantonal Environmental Protection Agency (Amt für Umwelt / Office de l'environnement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Simplified environmental registration, no full EIA report required under the EIA Ordinance (UVPV/OEIE): the bakery and central kitchen falls below the Annex II thresholds (wastewater discharge below 3,000 m3/year, no groundwater or sensitive-zone crossing, no listed combustion plant); a municipal sewer connection permit and environmental self-declaration are nevertheless mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: grease-bearing effluents must be pre-treated through an approved fat separator and comply with cantonal sewer bylaws (pH 6.5-9.5, COD ≤ 1000 mg/l, TSS ≤ 400 mg/l, temperature ≤ 40°C at the connection point). Air emissions: natural-gas-fired bakery ovens must comply with LRV Art. 13 flue-gas limits, soot/particulates ≤ 0.1 g/m3; total VOC emissions remain below the 10 t/yr LRV trigger; odour and noise controls to be documented. Waste: food waste and grease residues separated and removed by certified recyclers per the VVEA/OTD regulated-waste regime.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory approval by the cantonal or municipal fire prevention office (Feuerpolizei) of the escape routes, fire alarm system, and extinguishing plan; structural-load certificate by an approved engineer verifying floors and foundations for tiled ovens and central-kitchen equipment; occupational safety clearance by an EKAS-recognized consultant covering dust and flour handling, noise protection, heat exposure, ventilation rates (minimum 8 air changes per hour in the bakery hall), and an emergency first-aid protocol. Fire safety certification and workplace clearance are conditions precedent to the issuance of the operating license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC); official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch. The ESTV administers Federal Direct Tax, Swiss VAT registration and VAT returns; cantonal and communal profit/capital taxes are administered by the competent cantonal tax administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung / Administration fiscale cantonale) at the AG's registered seat.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) in the Swiss commercial register (Handelsregisteramt) to obtain the Swiss company number and the statutory Swiss Business Identification Number (UID / IDE / IDI) issued under the ZEFIX central name index (format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx; verified at www.uid.admin.ch). (2) Register the AG with the competent cantonal tax administration to obtain the cantonal corporate tax file number covering Federal Direct Tax and cantonal/communal taxes, and file the statutory articles of incorporation and board confirmation. (3) Apply to the ESTV for VAT registration (Mehrwertsteuer-Register) through the official Federal VAT e-portal by submitting the commercial register excerpt, founding deed, articles of association, and Swiss registered-office confirmation; the 9-digit UID then serves as the VAT identification number with the suffix MWST. (4) For foreign entities without a Swiss registered seat that nevertheless perform taxable supplies in Switzerland, a Swiss fiscal representative (ficcalischer Vertreter / representant fiscal) must be formally appointed and joined to the VAT registration, unless turnover from Swiss-source supplies remains below the statutory threshold. (5) Final step: ongoing annual filing of Federal Direct Tax returns, cantonal/communal tax returns, and VAT returns (quarterly or semi-annually), with financial statements prepared under Swiss Code of Obligations Arts. 958 ff.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Swiss AG is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to unlimited (world-wide) tax liability on its profits at Federal, cantonal and communal level (combined effective tax rate approximately 11.9%-21.0% depending on canton and profit volume); profits attributable to a foreign permanent establishment and income from foreign real estate are exempt from Swiss tax under the object-based exemption principle. The AG is not a pass-through entity; no tax-exempt zone treatment applies, and capital tax (Kapitalsteuer) is levied on paid-in share capital and statutory reserves. Non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of the shares without affecting entity-level taxation, subject to substance and arm's-length requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections and tax regimes include: (i) VAT group election (Mehrwertsteuer-Gruppierung, Art. 11 Federal VAT Act) consolidating economically, financially and organisationally integrated entities into a single Swiss VAT taxpayer; (ii) participation deduction election (Beteiligungsabzug) for qualifying dividends and capital gains; (iii) Swiss principal company advanced tax ruling enabling the central procurement, financing and risk-bearing functions of a master-franchise group to be compensated on a cost-plus basis after approval by the ESTV and the cantonal tax administration; (iv) reduced input-taxation flat-rate method (Saldosteuersatzverfahren) for smaller taxpayers; (v) de minimis non-subjectivity election for small social/non-profit entities; (vi) shareholder-level partial taxation procedure (Teilbesteuerungsverfahren) for dividend distributions; and (vii) thin-capitalisation safe-harbour ratios accepted as an administrative election. Hybrid mismatch consequences are addressed through Swiss treaty tie-breaker rules, substance-based anti-avoidance principles and BEPS-aligned deduction limitations; no domestic hybrid-mismatch check-the-box mechanism exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Federal Value Added Tax / Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA) governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (SR 641.20) and its implementing ordinances; administered by the ESTV.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 general threshold: compulsory Swiss VAT registration arises when worldwide annual turnover from taxable supplies, exclusive of VAT and duties, exceeds CHF 100,000 in a 12-month measurement period; a CHF 50,000 threshold applies to non-profit, social, public-law and pension-fund taxpayers; foreign entities register on Swiss-source taxable turnover exceeding CHF 100,000. For the bakery/Chinese-pastry chain, takeaway sales of bread, pastries and staple foodstuffs are taxable at the reduced rate of 2.6%, whereas in-premises café or table-service consumption is a restaurant service taxable at the standard rate of 8.1%; voluntary registration is available for Swiss real-estate owners and for businesses requiring input-VAT neutrality.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate real-time fiscal-clearance APIs, transaction-by-transaction tax-authority approval, or digital stamping. Since 30 June 2020 the Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is mandatory on all payment-slip invoices drawn on Swiss payment accounts. E-invoicing is permitted on a voluntary basis using the Swiss EBill standard, SIX Corporate EBill or Peppol-BIS 3.0 format, provided authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility are guaranteed and the invoice meets the mandatory content requirements of Art. 26 VAT Act. Invoices and underlying records must be retained for 10 years in a Swiss auditable archive. Export declarations are processed electronically through the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS / BAZG) e-dec web and NCTS interfaces, which is a customs-clearance function rather than a fiscal-stamping mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for the 0% VAT rate where ownership in goods (including central-kitchen product dispatches, fresh pastries, packaged Chinese pastry lines and bakery equipment) transfers to a foreign buyer and the goods are physically transported out of the Swiss customs territory to a destination abroad, evidenced by a release of the Swiss customs export declaration. Services qualify for the 0% rate where the recipient is a foreign master franchisee or affiliate with its business seat outside Switzerland and the place of supply of the service is determined as abroad pursuant to the recipient-location rule; this covers master franchise royalties, licence fees, central-kitchen operation and management fees, technology-transfer fees and logistics services, provided the service is not effectively used or enjoyed in Switzerland. Input VAT incurred on export-related purchases (raw ingredients, packaging, ovens, refrigeration, energy and logistics) is fully deductible against output VAT, and any excess credit is refunded either through the periodic VAT return or, for foreign unregistered entrepreneurs, through the ESTV refund procedure for foreign businesses.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung) released by the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS / BAZG) via e-dec web or NCTS, showing the Swiss exporter, foreign consignee, goods description, weight and exit confirmation
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR international consignment note evidencing physical movement of the goods across the Swiss border to the foreign franchisee
Commercial invoice and underlying sales contract / purchase order confirming the supply terms, title transfer and export destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103/MT202 or Swiss bank credit advice) evidencing repatriation and receipt of export proceeds into Switzerland within the prescribed 180-day period
Export schedule / zero-rating listing (Liste Z / Verzeichnis) annexed to the Swiss VAT return reconciling zero-rated sales with customs exit declarations

For export of services: written franchise or service agreement, evidence of the foreign recipient's registered seat (commercial-register excerpt), proof of actual service performance and evidence that the service is not used in Switzerland
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The FOCBS and ESTV systematically cross-match customs exit declarations, transport documents, VAT return export listings and inward foreign-exchange remittance records. Missing, incomplete or inconsistent export or FX documentation triggers denial of the 0% rate, retrospective reassessment at the standard rate, input VAT clawback, statutory default interest, and recovery actions against the Swiss AG and its responsible directors. Where fraudulent zero-rating or deliberate misdeclaration is established, criminal prosecution follows under Arts. 104 ff. of the Federal VAT Act with fines of up to three times the evaded tax, possible custodial sentence pursuant to the Swiss Criminal Code in aggravated tax-fraud cases, joint and several liability of the board of directors and the Swiss fiscal representative of any foreign parent entity, and cancellation or suspension of the VAT registration. The statutory retention and reassessment period of 10 years preserves long-tail audit exposure over all export transactions in the contested accounting periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB), Berne, acting as the independent central bank under the National Bank Act 2003, with banking supervision delegated to the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA). Switzerland maintains no separate foreign-exchange administration body; exchange-control policy is fully liberalized within SNB monetary policy parameters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc (CHF) is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are zero legal restrictions on foreign direct investment, dividend distributions, royalty remittances, loan servicing, or repatriation of liquidation proceeds, provided the transaction is lawful under Swiss private law and bank compliance protocols are satisfied. No Swiss Federal Council ordinance or SNB directive imposes prior approval for convertibility; the only practical gatekeepers are banks' own KYC/AML controls and reporting obligations under the Money Laundering Act (GwG), the Sanctions Act (Embargo Act), and the Automatic Exchange of Information (AEOI) framework. Profit remittance of a Swiss AG (Aktiengesellschaft) requires a valid annual general meeting (AGM) appropriation resolution and withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) of 35% on dividends unless reduced under the Switzerland-China double taxation agreement (rate reduced to 10% for qualifying shareholdings, and to 5% where beneficial owner holds at least 25% share capital). Royalties and management fees are subject to no Swiss withholding tax when paid cross-border, provided they comply with arm's-length transfer pricing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio to CHF for foreign-currency receipts. Exporters may retain, invest, or convert foreign currency freely. The only compliance layer arises from tax reporting (safe-keeping of invoice and SWIFT records for transfer-pricing audits) and from bank-level monitoring of large cash flows under GwG due-diligence thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CHF multi-currency corporate package) + Capital Escrow Account for paid-in share capital; dedicated Corporate Treasury Line for cross-border trade settlements
Operational Account and Escrow Account; cantonal banking relationship advantageous for entity registered in Canton Zurich; provides SIC/euroSIC clearing, merchant acquiring, and trade finance desk
Operational Account; strong regional SME coverage with approved external-asset-manager referral channels for non-resident directors
Operational Account; relevant if the central kitchen and franchise operations register in Canton Vaud; digital onboarding for SMEs with moderate cross-border volume
Operational Account (retail/SME); acceptable for low-risk bakery franchise cash operations and POS settlements, but limited trade-finance product suite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary payment orchestration, Low as the sole treasury backbone. FINMA-licensed fintech companies operating under the FinTech Licence (Art. 1b Banking Act) or as registered payment institutions under the Financial Institutions Act (FINIA) may provide e-money and payment initiation services, but none currently offer the full commercial banking stack (escrow account, guarantee instruments, LC issuing, and SIC settlement) required by a bakery master-franchise central kitchen. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK- or Lithuania-licensed payment firms) are generally prohibited from holding Swiss Client accounts in CHF unless they obtain a FINMA licence; Swiss banks will not clear mandates to unlicensed EMIs, and such EMIs cannot issue Swiss IBANs (CH32/CH93). Recommended architecture: use a tier-1 Swiss bank for treasury and combine with a regulated EMI (e.g., a FINMA-licensed fintech) solely for customer-facing POS and refund channels after obtaining written approval from the relationship bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINMA Circular 2016/07 and Art. 3 GwG require the identification of the beneficial owner via (i) the presentation of the original or certified-copy passport of each director and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), and (ii) a signed due-diligence self-declaration. Most Swiss tier-1 and cantonal banks mandate at least one on-site interview of the authorized signatory director at the Swiss branch for new corporate clients with non-EEA ultimate ownership; remote video identification is generally accepted for the co-signatories only. For an entity whose shareholder is a Chinese-resident individual, the mandatory in-person meeting at the bank's head office or in a Swiss consulate with a bank-certified notary is overwhelmingly the industry practice; a purely remote account opening is a reputational impracticability rather than a legal prohibition. We recommend the non-executive Swiss director or a fiduciary with a Swiss power of attorney attend the initial interview, with the beneficial owner available by teleconference, and a full original set of corporate documents certified by the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister) provided at the same session.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA / China-resident ultimate beneficial owner with a bakery franchisor in China creating perceived source-of-wealth opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport, residential proof, Chinese tax residence certificate (residencia fiscal), source-of-wealth report showing accumulated franchise profits and investment capital, bank references from two Chinese banks (e.g., ICBC and China Merchant Bank) with an explanation of prior company bank references, declaration of no PEP status, and a Swiss registered-office certificate with a signed mandate to a licensed Swiss fiduciary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cash turnover and daily POS settlements at retail bakery outlets triggering structured-transaction suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Terminal acquiring agreement with a Swiss certified payment provider (e.g., SIX Payment Services), a documented cash-management policy with daily deposit threshold and armed transit procedures, monthly POS-cash reconciliation templates, audited annual financial statements of the master-franchise company, and a nil-politically-exposed-person certificate for the operating subsidiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty and central-kitchen procurement payments to China flagged as potential money-laundering conduits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master-franchise agreement with defined royalty mechanics (percentage of net turnover), an intercompany transfer-pricing policy documented under OECD TP guidelines with a Swiss CMA functional analysis, purchase orders and HL invoices for Chinese specialty ingredients, and a schedule of actual counterparty bank details held on the approved vendor list certified by the CFO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purpose ambiguity for inbound capital payment (share capital contribution) leading to rejection under FINMA's 'transparent purpose' rule
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized share issuance resolution for the AG, Handelsregister excerpt evidencing the registered share capital (minimum CHF 100,000, at least CHF 50,000 paid in), an escrow instruction letter to the bank from the board, and the Articles of Association showing the bakery-franchise business purpose; funds will carry the SWIFT code 'CAPI' (capital contribution) or 'RESC' per Swiss payment purpose code conventions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection from the Chinese franchisor/shareholder must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the Chinese remitting bank to the Swiss beneficiary account, using the payment purpose code 'CAPI' (Capital) or 'ETPP' (Equity Transfer) when routed through the SIC/euroSIC. The routing protocol is: (i) the Swiss bank must be pre-advised with a board resolution and a capital-contribution confirmation signed by the COO; (ii) the remittance should originate from the shareholder's own corporate account and not a personal account to avoid third-party-payment strain; (iii) the advising bank and beneficiary bank SWIFT BIC must match the account relationship; (iv) the credit must be posted by close of business T+1, and the bank will issue a SchKG attestation if requested for commercial purposes; and (v) once credited, the funds are to be booked against the company's share-capital and legal reserves accounts, requiring subsequent shareholder meeting minutes. For trade pre-payments from the Chinese franchisor for central-kitchen equipment, use purpose code 'GOODS' or the ISO 20022 'Purpose' element 'TRAD' and ensure the invoice references the underlying purchase order; the Swiss bank will request the source-of-funds declaration where the amount exceeds CHF 50,000, and EDP application for the capital contribution is irrelevant given no Swiss withholding tax applies on paid-in capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For central-kitchen procurement from China and royalty/franchise fee disbursements to the Chinese master licensor, the cleanest clearing rail is (i) SWIFT MT103 for non-documentary payments cleared through SIC/euroSIC into CNY via a Chinese clearing bank or a correspondent bank in Hong Kong (e.g., Bank of China (Switzerland) AG as an offshore RMB clearing participant); and (ii) a commercial letter of credit (L/C) at sight (UCP 600) issued by the Swiss relationship bank in favour of the Chinese supplier, with documents to be negotiated through a nominated Chinese advising bank. For recurring royalty payments, we recommend a standing instruction with a direct debit mandate in favour of the Chinese licensor, executed on the 5th business day of each month, each payment limited to the contractually agreed royalty ceiling and the purpose code 'ROYA'. For large equipment procurement, an import documentary collection (D/P sight) provides cost-efficient settlement without bank financing exposure. The bank will require a copy of each underlying invoice, the transportation bill of lading or airway bill, and a certificate of origin for food-grade bakery equipment to satisfy Swiss import and Chinese export compliance; all payments above CHF 50,000 are subject to the bank's transaction monitoring and may trigger a request for the corresponding trade contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (CHF/CNY, CHF/EUR, CHF/USD) with tenors up to 24 months executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a short-form FX Master Agreement with the relationship bank; documenting the underlying commercial exposure (royalties, procurement) is required for bank approval.

FX swaps (swap of principal and interest cash-flows between CHF and CNY/EUR) permissible for rolling-over settlement exposures on the central-kitchen procurement cycle, provided the swap is entered for hedging, not speculative open positions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY where counterparty provides an offshore CNY fixing (CNH) benchmark; permissible for a Swiss-resident company hedging CNY-settled trade flows; the Swiss bank will require evidence that the CNH/CNY mismatch is referenced to a recognized fixing (e.g., China Foreign Exchange Trade System 4.30pm fix) and will run a pre-netting MTM margin.

Vanilla FX options (call or put on CHF against CNY/EUR/USD) as premium-based hedging instruments, permitted without prospectus requirements when sold by the bank to a professional client under FINMA's client-classification rules; prohibited strategies include binary barriers and leveraged accumulators unless the company qualifies as per se professional and signs a risk disclosure.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for long-dated matched funding from China, permitted only with a licensed Swiss bank counterparty and subject to standard collateral arrangements under the Swiss Master Agreement for OTC derivative transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and General Meeting Package (balance sheet, income statement, notes, distribution proposal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt) and shareholders at the Annual General Meeting; tax authorities receive a copy for assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end (Art. 958f OR); for calendar-year AGs, by 30 June; corporate tax return usually due 31 March/30 April depending on canton
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission triggers default interest and tax penalties; persistent non-compliance may lead to court-ordered forced deregistration under Art. 938 OR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Federal, Cantonal and Communal Corporate Income Tax Return including Capital Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority on behalf of the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, 31 March or extended 30 April (cantonal variation); further extensions available upon reasoned request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest starts after the deadline and late-payment penalties can reach up to 30% of assessed tax; deliberate concealment invokes penal tax proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT (MWST) Periodic or Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV, VAT Division)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after end of the VAT settlement period; annual settlement no later than 60 days after 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 3.5% p.a. (adjustable); penalties up to 4x the tax amount in cases of gross negligence and denial of input VAT deduction in persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register Filing of Audited or Reviewed Annual Accounts (where audit is not waived)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt); public electronic notice through Swiss Official Gazette (SHAB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance-sheet date, accompanied by the statutory audit/review report if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an administrative offence; registrar may issue a final reminder and proceed with filing at company expense, followed by judicial deregistration in repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO / Beneficial Owner Register Annual Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at company registered office; available upon request to Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS), FINMA, and cantonal authorities; not a public filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation at incorporation anniversary and within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; records must reflect current ownership at 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Misdemeanour under anti-money laundering rules and Art. 325ter Criminal Code; fines up to CHF 100,000 and personal liability of directors for inaccurate disclosure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Registers Reconciliation and Corporate Minute Book Audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal compliance records produced on demand to statutory auditors, tax authorities, and notaries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed before the Annual General Meeting and no later than 30 June for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective registers constitute a corporate-governance breach; courts may order rectification under Art. 937 OR, and audit reports may carry adverse findings affecting credit and licensing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit under Art. 727 OR when a company exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total CHF 20 million, annual turnover CHF 40 million, 250 full-time employees; also mandatory for listed companies, companies with bearer shares, and certain regulated entities. Limited audit/review required where any two of three lower thresholds are exceeded (balance sheet CHF 4 million, turnover CHF 8 million, 50 employees); companies with fewer than 10 employees may be exempted by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR Arts. 957-963e); Swiss GAAP FER applicable for medium and large entities; consolidated accounts may use IFRS or US GAAP for internationally listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss non-listed AGs must identify natural-person beneficial owners and maintain a Beneficial Owner Register on site. Confirmation is performed annually, and any share transfer or change of control must be reported into the register within 30 days. The company must also provide a written UBO declaration to its financial intermediary, trustee, or notary when opening accounts or executing major transactions; non-compliance blocks dividends and can invalidate bearer-share rights.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Officers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500 - $8,500 for limited review; $10,000 - $30,000 for ordinary statutory audit

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Official tax return form designation and electronic filing system
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline relative to the fiscal year-end
